role: Image forensics: locate and electrically classify the suspected screenshot short

directChecks.result: Matched two close upper vias, diagonal-versus-vertical crossing, lower bends, and neighboring OVLO/discharge/via geometry to inner2 upper-left region.
pcb_trace_193 route segment (-29.167,23.108)→(-24.525,27.75) intersects pcb_trace_246 vertical (-25.638,14.874)→(-25.638,27.75) at (-25.638,26.637) mm. Both 0.2 mm wide; centerline separation is 0.

Both connected_source_net_ids=[source_net_1], source_net_1.name=V3V3; both connectivity_map_key=...net81. Source logicSupplyConnectionPlans ALERT_VCC_LINK explicitly net V3V3; this is the supply side of two pull-up resistors, not PD_ALERT signal.

71 inner2 trace-segment/via primitives, 2255 foreign-net pairs, zero overlaps. Trace centerline separation calculated with Shapely exact segment distance, subtracting trace half-width/via radius. Region [-36,10,-18,30] mm. No inner2 pours exist.
V3V3 pcb_via_87 to INPUT_OVLO pcb_trace_360 edge clearance 0.2284762339242242 mm, versus configured 0.2 mm trace-to-pad margin. Positive margin 0.028476 mm.

Minimum copper ring gap 0.18153332324989546 mm between PD_ALERT pcb_via_164 and GND pcb_via_379. Their 0.3 mm drills are 0.581533 mm edge-to-edge, above board 0.3 mm minimum drill spacing. Two other positive via-via ring gaps are 0.194427 and 0.194930 mm. The board does not define a general 0.2 mm via-to-via copper-edge minimum; these are not reported as configured-rule failures.
Reconstructed SVG/PNG from exact CJS wire coordinates and via diameters. Highlighted the two V3V3 traces and their four vias without modifying geometry.

strengths: The apparent screenshot contact has verified same-net source semantics, so it is electrically legitimate.
Local foreign copper stays physically separated; the V3V3/INPUT_OVLO approach clears the configured 0.2 mm trace-to-pad value.
The pictured branches use a consistent 0.2 mm signal/supply width and explicit four-layer plated vias.

findings.explanation: The visible diagonal/vertical contact is a real copper junction of V3V3. It is not a foreign-net short. ALERT_INNER2_TRUNK is a misleadingly named VCC distribution trace, not the alert signal.

The two upper V3V3 vias return separately through top-layer traces to the same R_INPUT_FAULT.pin1 while the inner2 paths already join below them. This creates a small redundant two-layer copper loop. It is electrically benign in this low-current pull-up supply, but a single shared junction/via could make intent clearer and use less copper/drilling if source-route constraints are updated and revalidated.

evidence.interpretation: Measured closed planar routing cycle; optimization feasibility inferred and unvalidated.

findings.explanation: Some regional via rings are separated by less than 0.2 mm, but remain positive and meet the configured drill-to-drill spacing. The V3V3-via to INPUT_OVLO trace margin above 0.2 mm is only 0.0285 mm. These dimensions should be carried into the eventual fabrication-rule review; they do not establish a short or a configured-rule violation.

suspectedShortAssessment.scope: The localized screenshot region and exact CJS trace/via primitives; no claim about whole-board Gerber or physical hardware.

topImprovements: Rename ALERT_INNER2_TRUNK to a supply-explicit name so reviewers do not mistake it for PD_ALERT.
Consider consolidating the redundant upper V3V3 feed into one intentional junction/via with connectivity, clearance and source-route constraints rechecked.
Preserve quantified positive but narrow clearances in fabrication-rule review, instead of using angle lint as the quality score.
limitations: Overall score is a localized image-forensics perspective, with medium confidence across the entire board. The screenshot concern itself is resolved with high confidence.

This check covers inner2 CJS traces and via rings in the localized region, including full four-layer via projections. It does not check external pads, other layers, solder mask, exact Gerber apertures or fabrication tolerances.
No board build, routing mutation, physical measurement or fabrication export was performed.
